source: General Handout 5 - Skills Use Guideline, expanded with clearly labelled Therapy Skill Kit curriculum navigation

zones.name: Emotional overload
zones.description: Feelings or urges are very intense, and it may be hard to access Wise Mind.

skills.name: TIPP
skills.summary: Quick body-based methods for very high emotional arousal.
skills.best_for: Bringing intensity down enough to choose the next effective step.
skills.description: Temperature, intense exercise, paced breathing, and progressive muscle relaxation are crisis-survival options.

skills.name: ACCEPTS
skills.summary: Short-term ways to redirect attention during a crisis.
skills.best_for: Getting through a peak without making the situation worse.
skills.description: Choose a safe activity, contribution, comparison, opposite emotion, pushing away, thought, or sensation strategy.

skills.name: Self-Soothe
skills.summary: Use the senses to offer your body comfort and steadiness.
skills.best_for: Reducing distress through safe sensory care.
skills.description: Select a sight, sound, smell, taste, or touch that is safe and soothing.

skills.name: STOP
skills.summary: Pause, step back, observe, and proceed mindfully.
skills.best_for: Interrupting an impulsive reaction before acting.
skills.description: Create a brief pause so the next action can be chosen more deliberately.

skills.name: IMPROVE
skills.summary: Make a painful moment more bearable in the short term.
skills.best_for: Finding one workable way through a difficult moment.
skills.description: Use imagery, meaning, prayer, relaxation, one thing, vacation, or encouragement as appropriate.

skills.name: Opposite Action
skills.summary: Act opposite to an urge when the emotion does not fit the facts or acting would be ineffective.
skills.best_for: Changing an emotion through action, expression, and posture.
skills.description: Use the Change Emotion decision tree to check fit and effectiveness before choosing the action.

skills.name: Box Breathing
skills.summary: Use a configurable four-phase visual breathing timer.
skills.best_for: A structured breathing focus when it feels comfortable and useful.
skills.description: Set inhale, hold, exhale, and second-hold durations, then start, pause, or reset.

skills.name: Grounding
skills.summary: Reconnect with immediate sensory information, the body, and the environment.
skills.best_for: Feeling overwhelmed, unreal, disconnected, or pulled away from the present.
skills.description: Follow a concise, low-typing guided progression without a fabricated sensory count.

zones.name: Distressed but in Wise Mind
zones.description: Distress is present, and there is enough steadiness to reflect and choose deliberately.

skills.name: Pros & Cons
skills.summary: Compare short- and long-term effects of acting on a crisis urge.
skills.best_for: Strengthening commitment when two choices are pulling at you.
skills.description: Review consequences of acting and not acting before choosing deliberately.

skills.name: Problem Solving
skills.summary: Define a changeable problem, choose a solution, and test it.
skills.best_for: Emotions that fit a situation you can influence.
skills.description: Use the source steps to identify the problem, options, action, and review.

skills.name: Check the Facts
skills.summary: Separate observable facts from assumptions and interpretations.
skills.best_for: Checking whether an emotion and its intensity fit what is happening.
skills.description: Examine the event, interpretations, threat, catastrophe, and actual fit.

skills.name: Cope Ahead
skills.summary: Rehearse an effective plan for a difficult situation before it happens.
skills.best_for: Preparing for a predictable challenge while you can think clearly.
skills.description: Imagine the situation, choose effective skills, and rehearse coping in detail.

skills.name: Recognizing Thinking Traps
skills.summary: Identify interpretation habits that may be shaping a difficult thought.
skills.best_for: Creating enough distance to check a thought rather than accepting it automatically.
skills.description: Review the curriculum's twelve trap categories and select any that may fit.

skills.name: Thought Record
skills.summary: Examine a hot thought with evidence and build a balanced alternative.
skills.best_for: Working carefully with a recurring or emotionally charged automatic thought.
skills.description: Complete the source-backed Part 1 and Part 2 progression in one record.

skills.name: Worry Time
skills.summary: Postpone extended worry to an optional planned, limited period.
skills.best_for: Worry that repeatedly interrupts the day when immediate action is not needed.
skills.description: Note a brief cue, choose an optional worry-time window, and return to the present task.

skills.name: Positive Self-Talk
skills.summary: Develop a fair, believable, supportive response to a difficult thought.
skills.best_for: Self-critical thinking that can be examined without forced positivity.
skills.description: Use the best-friend and balanced-alternative framing already taught in the CBT curriculum.

zones.name: Wise Mind
zones.description: There is room to notice the whole situation and choose a skill intentionally.

skills.name: Interpersonal Effectiveness
skills.summary: Choose skills for objectives, relationships, and self-respect.
skills.best_for: Making a request, saying no, or navigating a relationship deliberately.
skills.description: Choose the most relevant DEAR MAN, GIVE, FAST, priority, or boundary material.

skills.name: Mindfulness of Emotions
skills.summary: Observe an emotion without suppressing it or automatically acting on it.
skills.best_for: Making space for a current emotion with awareness.
skills.description: Notice the emotion as a changing experience and return to effective action.

skills.name: Radical Acceptance
skills.summary: Acknowledge reality as it is when it cannot be changed right now.
skills.best_for: Reducing added suffering from fighting unchangeable facts.
skills.description: Practice turning the mind toward reality without approving of harm or giving up on change.

skills.name: Pleasant Activities
skills.summary: Intentionally make room for safe, realistic pleasant experiences.
skills.best_for: Building positive moments without demanding a particular mood.
skills.description: Browse the complete source activity list and make one event easier to follow through on.

skills.name: Five Factor Model
skills.summary: Map how a situation, thoughts, emotions, body sensations, and behaviours interact.
skills.best_for: Understanding a repeating pattern before choosing where to intervene.
skills.description: Describe all five source factors as an interacting loop rather than a one-way chain.

skills.name: Gratitude Journal
skills.summary: Record specific things you appreciate and what makes them meaningful.
skills.best_for: A small reflective practice when there is room to notice what matters.
skills.description: Add one or more entries without treating gratitude as a demand to feel better.

zones.name: Emotional numbness
zones.description: You feel disconnected, shut down, flat, or far away from emotion.

skills.name: Build Mastery
skills.summary: Do one achievable activity that builds competence over time.
skills.best_for: Creating momentum and a sense of capability in small steps.
skills.description: Choose an attainable challenge and build gradually rather than demanding a large change.

skills.name: PLEASE
skills.summary: Support emotional balance by caring for core physical needs.
skills.best_for: Checking illness care, eating, substances, sleep, and movement.
skills.description: Review body-care factors that can increase vulnerability when neglected.

skills.name: Grounding
skills.summary: Reconnect with immediate sensory information and the present environment.
skills.best_for: Feeling disconnected, unreal, shut down, or far away.
skills.description: Use large guided controls and minimal typing to orient through senses and body contact.

skills.name: Behavioural Activation
skills.summary: Choose one specific, manageable activity and make it easier to begin.
skills.best_for: Low energy, withdrawal, avoidance, or loss of routine.
skills.description: Select a source activity or your own action, identify barriers, and plan the smallest version.

skills.name: Pleasant Event Planner
skills.summary: Plan one safe pleasant event without waiting for motivation first.
skills.best_for: Reintroducing small positive or meaningful moments.
skills.description: Browse the source Pleasant Events List and schedule a realistic choice if useful.

skills.name: Gratitude Journal
skills.summary: Notice one specific appreciated detail without forcing a mood change.
skills.best_for: A gentle reflective practice when a small amount of noticing is possible.
skills.description: Record what you appreciate and why it matters, while leaving room for difficult experience.
